title: Telemetry intake & prioritization playbook for enterprise analytics and cost attribution
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Purpose: Define a repeatable intake and prioritization playbook for incoming enterprise requests related to telemetry, usage analytics, cost breakdowns, and ad-hoc exports so PM/Eng/Design can triage consistently and meet enterprise SLAs.

Scope: Console-facing reporting, CSV/Parquet exports, API endpoints for usage and cost attribution, per-workspace or per-customer dashboards, one-off analytics jobs for contract compliance. Excludes core billing ingestion pipelines and outage incident telemetry (handled by infra).

Required intake fields (minimum set):
- Requestor name, company, and workspace ID
- Business objective and customer-facing impact statement (1-2 sentences)
- Desired deliverable (dashboard / export / new metric / SLA report)
- Data scope (time window, models/routes, token granularity, labels/tags)
- Security classification (public | internal | regulated)
- Expected frequency (one-time | daily | weekly | ad-hoc)
- Acceptance criteria / sample output (CSV header or mock dashboard)

Scoring rubric (0-5 each, total 0-25):
- Business value (revenue recovery, upsell, renewal risk)
- Frequency of request (how often customer will use it)
- Number of affected customers/workspaces
- Engineering complexity (integration, infra changes, retrofitting datasets)
- Security/regulatory effort (PII, compliance, export controls)

Prioritization bands:
- Priority A (>=16): assign next sprint; commercial engagement + SLA; ship within 4 weeks and offer interim workaround.
- Priority B (10-15): consider next two cycles; prototype and validate; product review required.
- Priority C (<10): backlog; provide self-serve guidance or partner with solutions engineering for one-off delivery.

Routing rules:
- If security classification == regulated OR customer tier == enterprise with contract clause => require security review and route to Private Deployments/Legal early.
- If request impacts per-token billing accuracy or exposes differential cost allocation => flag Finance + Billing infra and mark "high" for customer_impact.
- If request requests new telemetry that requires upstream schema changes => create dependency to ENG and estimate separately.

Artifacts required before design kickoff:
- Completed intake form and sample output
- Customer business sponsor confirmation (email or signed note)
- Data availability check (Telemetry owner must confirm presence of required fields in analytics tables)

Acceptance criteria (examples):
- Fresh export generation within SLA (e.g., daily export completes <4 hours for 30-day window)
- Dashboard shows per-customer token & cost breakdown with filters by model and route
- Export schema documented with column definitions, PII flags, and retention notes

Operational SLAs and communication plan:
- Triage acknowledgement: within 3 business days
- Initial scope/design proposal: within 10 business days for Priority A/B
- Regular cadence: weekly updates for active enterprise requests; central tracking in the Console Requests board

Metrics to track success:
- Time-to-triage, time-to-design, time-to-delivery
- % of enterprise requests delivered within SLA
- NPS change for requesting customers after delivery
- Reduction in duplicate ad-hoc requests (measure consolidation)

Open trade-offs and decisions needed:
- Granularity vs. cost: per-token, per-inference attribution increases storage and compute; recommended default is per-route + sampled per-customer token-level only for high-value contracts.
- Self-serve vs. managed: many requests start as one-offs; consider adding a self-serve export builder in Console to lower operational load.
- Long-term data platform vs. short-term ETL: build minimal ETL for quick wins, but define a roadmap dependency for scalable analytics platform.

Next steps:
1) Approve playbook and intake form template (PM + Legal + Security)
2) Build intake form in Zendesk/Confluence + automation to create Linear ticket with pre-filled labels
3) Pilot with top 3 enterprise customers for two months and collect acceptance metrics

Why this is different from current reporting docs: This playbook focuses on enterprise-facing telemetry requests that are time-sensitive and contractually relevant (cost attribution, audit exports), not generic usage dashboards. It includes a quantified scoring rubric and explicit routing rules for security and billing dependencies.

acceptance_criteria: See description section 'Acceptance criteria (examples)'. Deliverables must include schema, performance verification, and customer sign-off.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Pilot with 3 customers and feature-flagged exports in Console; Phase 2: General availability for enterprise seats with opt-in; Phase 3: Surface self-serve builder for select non-regulated exports.
notes: Keep a registry of ad-hoc exports and map them to reusable queries/components to avoid rework. Coordinate with Solutions Eng for initial deliveries.
